selected_modules.reason: The bug is a C++-only regression in -Woverloaded-virtual on multiple inheritance, and the reproducer tests are all under g++.dg/warn. This warning depends on C++ class hierarchy, name lookup, overload/hiding, virtual function semantics, and front-end warning issuance, all of which are centered in the C++ front end.

The issue is explicitly a warning/diagnostic regression (-Woverloaded-virtual, -Wall). Shared C-family warning/diagnostic infrastructure is a plausible location for option-controlled warning handling and common front-end diagnostic behavior used by C++.

The report mentions warning option forms including -Woverloaded-virtual and -Woverloaded-virtual=2, indicating possible involvement of option parsing, warning level handling, and propagation of warning settings into the front end.

Observed behavior is a false positive warning emission. While the semantic decision is likely in the C++ front end, GCC’s diagnostics subsystem is relevant for warning classification, formatting, and suppression behavior.

If the regression is not purely in front-end lookup, it may involve shared tree-level representation of methods, inheritance, and virtual dispatch metadata consumed by the C++ front end when deciding whether a virtual is hidden.

Less likely than cp, but included as a shared IR/lowering module because some C-family/C++ warnings can be influenced by front-end lowering or generic tree/GIMPLE utilities. Still secondary since no middle-end pass is implicated.

This broad core module includes common option/pass framework and generic compiler infrastructure. It is a fallback candidate for shared warning plumbing or regression-causing core changes not confined to cp.

Included only as a lower-probability shared middle-end candidate. The pass trace shows normal tree/rtl pipelines, but the issue is a compile-time warning with no pass-local evidence, so this is unlikely but possible if warning state is affected by SSA/tree analyses.

Multiple inheritance warning logic is unlikely to be CFG-based, but this is a low-probability shared analysis substrate candidate if some diagnostic path inspection or function-body structure affected warning issuance.

Virtual function and class hierarchy reasoning can sometimes touch global callgraph/devirtualization infrastructure, though for -Woverloaded-virtual this is much less likely than cp. Included as a distant possibility due to virtual-related metadata handling.
